statement: In the sybil-cone scenario, guarantor-XP coupling raises the attacker coalition's Council seat share, the amplification requires coalition-level guarantee intensity, and it is not produced by the attackers' higher Self-ID rate.

claims.rationale: XP never feeds back into agent behavior, so under shared replica seeds the two arms have identical populations and graphs; the contrast isolates the XP-coupling rule's effect on seats.
Difference-in-differences: lowering attacker guarantee intensity to the honest rate (2 to 0.3 proposals per subject-day) removes most of the amplification.
With attacker Self-ID probability equal to the honest 0.8, coupling still amplifies seat share.

alternatives.explanation: The attackers' higher scripted Self-ID probability (1.0 versus 0.8) alone creates the extra guarantor XP.
